principles: Categories overlap and are not exhaustive.
Assess context-specific instances; do not put company facts in this catalog.
Select one leading focus while retaining all other constraints.
A category suggests questions, not a mandatory action.
Authority and consent are admissibility conditions across categories.
Local additions use x-<namespace>:<code>; global changes require a catalog version.

conditions.definition: Missing, stale, conflicting or unreliable evidence.
conditions.example: A funnel export predates a product change.

conditions.definition: Consequences remain uncertain and only partly controllable, even with better information.
conditions.example: A tested improvement may fail in a different cohort.

conditions.definition: Participants, goals or requirements pull toward incompatible choices.
conditions.example: Faster activation may conflict with support workload.

conditions.definition: Time, budget, attention, competence or prerequisites limit feasible action.
conditions.example: Two experiments need the same analyst during the same week.

conditions.definition: The context, agreement, needs or permissions have changed.
A method, actor or tool may be unable to perform the required action reliably.
conditions.example: The tool fails or the employee lacks the required domain competence.
